text: All the manifold complex of differences, such as the enjoyer and the enjoyed, other than that [the Absolute], are imagined in it through ignorance. Those who, relying on the authority of a collection of statements such as "O Soma, in the beginning, this was that alone, one without a second" (Chandogya 6.2.1) and hundreds of other primary scriptural texts such as "the knower of the Self crosses over sorrow" (Chandogya 7.1.3), acknowledge the removal of ignorance through the knowledge of the non-dual oneness of the attributeless Brahman and the Self, and who, by hearing the condemnation of difference—as in "he attains a death worse than death who sees only difference here" (Katha 2.1)—consider the negation of ultimate difference to be the mark of the discerning, cannot tolerate this division.
